title: 7. Tenure and Qualifications of Council Members

blocks.content: The Legislative Council is a permanent body and not subject to dissolution, but one-third of its members retire every second year.

items: Minimum age for Vidhan Parishad is 30 years, compared to 25 years for Vidhan Sabha.
Parliament alone has the authority to prescribe additional qualifications for membership under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
Disqualification on grounds of defection under the 10th Schedule is decided by the Chairman of the Legislative Council.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Legislative Council is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution.
Members serve a term of six years, with one-third of the total members retiring every second year.
A candidate must be a citizen of India and at least 30 years of age to be eligible for election to the Council.
Additional qualifications and disqualifications are determined by Parliament under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
